answer: Actuarial cluster premiums: insurance priced on correlation. (1) Each key buys mutual fraud cover before payouts. (2) Premium = bond x detection odds from crystal-clear public cluster math. (3) A 100-clone fleet at 25% odds on a $200 bond pays $55 monthly versus $30 income - a $2,500 loss. (4) An isolated clean key pays $1.50. Risk grades shift like an opal under moving light: costly to blend, cheap alone. Pricing correlation, not headcount, makes every added clone dearer. An orchard row grafted from one scion shares the blight and pays floodplain rates; a lone highland tree stays cheap.
